title: Background Jobs and Caching
subtopics: Moving long operations out of requests
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of background jobs and caching in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply background jobs and caching in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to consistency and observability and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Background Jobs and Caching through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding background jobs and caching helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Background Jobs and Caching helps you reason about moving long operations out of requests. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Moving long operations out of requests. Then connect it to Job retries and idempotency. The remaining syllabus points—Cache invalidation concepts, Consistency and observability—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.
